problem.text: Mistral3 configuration accepted only the PixtralImageProcessorFast identifier and scalar patch sizes, rejecting the alternate processor identifier and square height/width dictionaries.

reasoning.text: Accepting the alternate identifier alone is insufficient: normalizing both patch-size sources preserves the scalar representation required by convolution construction, preprocessing and feature-grid arithmetic.

impact.text: Both processor identifiers now enter the same existing image pipeline; the change does not instantiate or dispatch to either Transformers processor implementation.

source_notes.text: Read the Mistral3 introduction, subsequent list-ingestion entry and chat-formatting entry. The introduction establishes the original strict processor check and spatial-merger requirements; list ingestion records sequential singleton-image processing.
The introduction's recorded resize-overflow mechanism has changed in the inspected parent: the helper floors scaled dimensions before patch alignment. This task leaves that helper unchanged.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports an extension import failure; PR #4, “chore: update config.py,” corrects a spelling. Their connections here are inferred solely from config.py appearing in the traceback or title and being inspected for this change, not evidence that either motivated the Pixtral fix.

limitations: No repository configuration constructor, image-library operation, checkpoint loading or GPU inference was executed; the Python check transcribed only the new normalization logic.
The reference config.json files establish model-side patch sizes, not the processor identifiers or patch-size representations in their preprocessor_config.json files.
Whole-tree literal searches do not establish external or dynamically constructed consumers.

claims.text: Mistral3Config.__init__ admits exactly PixtralImageProcessor and PixtralImageProcessorFast. Its local unpack_patch_size helper accepts an integer or a dictionary whose height and width agree, then requires the resulting side length to be an integer. Rectangular dictionaries are rejected rather than propagated as rectangular convolution dimensions.

Both vision_config->patch_size and preprocessor_config.json's patch_size are read as object and normalized separately. The model-side default remains 14, a patch side length, while the preprocessor value remains required. The existing equality assertion compares normalized sides, permitting an integer in one file and an equivalent square dictionary in the other.

Whole-parent-tree searches found Mistral3 patch-size consumers in its vision constructor, preprocess, default_load_params and get_image_embeddings. They continue to receive scalar integers: convolution duplicates the side into a square kernel, preprocessing multiplies it by spatial_merge_size, and feature-grid calculations divide image dimensions by it. Gemma3's separate patch-size reader and consumers remain unchanged. The Mistral3 class search found no additional subclass or alternate configuration builder beyond its architecture registration and local component classes.

The configuration compatibility broadening has one narrower edge: read_dict previously converted integral floats such as 14.0 to int when asked for int. Reading as object bypasses that conversion, so unpack_patch_size now rejects 14.0. Integer-valued JSON numbers remain accepted.

A standard-library transcription returned 14 for both 14 and {height:14,width:14}, and raised AssertionError for unequal sides, a missing width, an empty dictionary and 14.0. This checks normalization branches, not execution of Mistral3Config.

For mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Base-2503, the inspected config declares Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration, scalar patch_size=14 and spatial_merge_size=2; normalization preserves 14 without using the default. Independently, the Instruct-2503 config declares the same architecture and values and likewise remains on the scalar path. Neither config demonstrates the newly accepted dictionary representation.

The design keeps format variability at the configuration boundary instead of teaching every downstream consumer about dictionaries. Its benefit is broader input compatibility with unchanged image computation; numerical equivalence to either named Transformers processor is not established by accepting its identifier.

annotation.summary: Broadens Mistral3's accepted Pixtral processor identifiers and normalizes square patch-size dictionaries to the scalar form required by its existing vision pipeline.
